definitions.explanation: The physical eyeball. Also used in the expression {目玉|めだま}が{飛|と}び{出|で}る (eyes pop out) to express extreme surprise or shock at a price.
The most attractive or attention-grabbing item or feature, especially in sales, events, or plans.

examples.japanese: {目玉焼|めだまや}きを{作|つく}った。
{値段|ねだん}を{見|み}て{目玉|めだま}が{飛|と}び{出|で}た。
examples.english: My eyes popped out when I saw the price.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{大|おお}きな{目玉|めだま}をくりくりさせて{不思議|ふしぎ}そうに{見|み}ていた。
examples.english: The child was looking on curiously with big, round eyes.

examples.japanese: セールの{目玉|めだま}{商品|しょうひん}はテレビだ。
examples.english: The featured item in the sale is a TV.

examples.japanese: この{企画|きかく}の{目玉|めだま}は{何|なん}ですか。
examples.english: What is the highlight of this project?

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}の{予算案|よさんあん}の{目玉|めだま}は、{子育|こそだ}て{支援|しえん}の{大幅|おおはば}な{拡充|かくじゅう}だ。
examples.english: The centerpiece of this budget proposal is a major expansion of childcare support.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1: {目玉焼|めだまや}き (fried egg, literally "eyeball fry") is a very common compound. The expression {目玉|めだま}が{飛|と}び{出|で}る ({値段|ねだん}) means the price is shockingly high.

Sense 2: Used as a modifier, {目玉|めだま}{商品|しょうひん} (featured product) is standard retail language.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目玉焼|めだまや}き: fried egg (sunny-side up)
- {目玉|めだま}{商品|しょうひん}: featured product, loss leader
- {目玉|めだま}が{飛|と}び{出|で}る: eyes pop out (from shock)
- {目玉|めだま}{企画|きかく}: featured project/event
